routes.name: national
routes.summary: National identity- and company-number validation, 23 countries
routes.description: Validate a national identity, tax or company registration number against its country's official checksum rule. Covers 23 countries including NL BSN, ES NIF/NIE/CIF, IT codice fiscale, FR SIREN/SIRET, DE Steuer-ID, BE/PL/CZ national numbers, SE/NO/DK/FI personal numbers, BR CPF/CNPJ, AU ABN/TFN, UK NINo, IE PPS, US NPI/EIN. Structure and check digit only — no registry lookup; the number itself is never stored (logs keep only its length and character types).

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, case-insensitive. One of the 23 supported countries; the United Kingdom is accepted as UK or GB (the response echoes what you sent).
params.expected: one of the 23 supported ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes

params.name: kind
params.description: Identifier type for that country, e.g. bsn, nif, cf, cpf.
params.expected: an identifier kind supported for the country

params.name: value
params.description: The identifier. Separators (space . - /) are stripped before checking.

routes.output: valid (boolean), country, kind, normalised (string|null), formatted (string|null), reason (null | length | charset | checksum | structure | reserved_range: a number in a range the issuer reserves or never assigned, e.g. CA SIN starting 0 or 8, UK NINO prefixes BG GB KN NK NT TN ZZ, US EIN unassigned prefixes, NZ IRD outside 10,000,000-150,000,000), algorithm (e.g. elfproef-11, mod-97-10, luhn), derived (object of facts the number encodes, {} when none: birth_date (YYYY-MM-DD) and sex (M|F) for IT cf, SE personnummer, PL pesel, BE rrn, NO fodselsnummer, DK cpr, FI hetu, CZ rc and SK rc; birthplace_code for IT cf; century_assumed (boolean) for SE personnummer, true when a 10-digit form forced the century to be inferred; for BE, NO, DK, FI, CZ and SK the number itself fixes the century (BE by the check digits, NO by the individual number, DK by the sequence digit, FI by the century sign, CZ/SK by the digit count). birth_date is omitted when the encoded date is not a real date, and for NO FH-numbers). FR nir carries no day and no century, so its derived holds sex, birth_year_yy (2 digits), birth_month (1-12, or null for special codes) and department_code instead of birth_date. normalised is the number without separators (SE personnummer keeps a 12-digit input's century and a + sign).

routes.name: gs1
routes.summary: GS1 identifier validation: GTIN-8/12/13/14, GLN, SSCC
routes.description: Validate and convert GS1 identifiers: GTIN-8, GTIN-12 (UPC-A), GTIN-13 (EAN-13), GTIN-14, GLN and SSCC. Returns the check-digit verdict, the computed correct check digit, the GTIN-14 form with its indicator digit, and conversion between GTIN-8, GTIN-12, GTIN-13 and GTIN-14. No company-prefix split is returned: GS1's prefix-length table is no longer public data. Also computes a missing check digit from a partial code. Structure only, no product database.

params.name: op
params.description: validate (default), checkdigit (compute the missing final digit) or convert.

params.name: value
params.description: GS1 code, digits with optional spaces or hyphens. For op=checkdigit, omit the final digit.

params.name: to
params.description: Target format. Required when op=convert.

routes.output: valid, type (gtin8|gtin12|gtin13|gtin14|gln|sscc|unknown), normalised, check_digit (the digit that should be there; string|null, null when the length is unsupported), check_digit_ok, gtin14 (zero-padded; string|null, null for sscc and unsupported lengths), indicator (string|null), reason (string|null), also_valid_as (present only for a gtin13, which is also a valid gln: [gln]; also after op=checkdigit and op=convert that produce a gtin13), converted (op=convert only: the value in the requested format; null when the input's check digit is wrong, in which case valid is false, reason is checksum and type and normalised are those of the input). The GS1 company-prefix boundary is not returned.

routes.name: security
routes.summary: ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL and FIGI check-digit validation
routes.description: Validate the check digit of a financial security identifier: ISIN (ISO 6166), CUSIP, SEDOL and FIGI. Returns the verdict, the computed correct check character, and for an ISIN the issuing country prefix and the embedded NSIN. Also builds an ISIN from a country code plus a 9-character NSIN. Format and checksum only, no security master lookup.

params.name: op
params.description: validate (default) or build-isin.

params.name: value
params.description: ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL or FIGI to validate. Required when op=validate.
params.expected: an alphanumeric security identifier of at most 24 characters

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or XS. Required when op=build-isin.

params.name: nsin
params.description: Exactly 9 alphanumeric characters. Required when op=build-isin.

routes.output: validate: valid, type (isin|cusip|sedol|figi|unknown), normalised, check_char (string|null, null when the type is unknown), check_char_ok, country (ISIN only; string|null), nsin (ISIN only; string|null), reason (string|null, null when valid), algorithm (string|null, null when the type is unknown). build-isin: isin plus the same fields.

routes.name: iban
routes.summary: IBAN validation: length, per-field character classes, mod-97-10, decomposed bank/branch/account
routes.description: Validate an IBAN: length for its country, permitted character classes per field, and the ISO 7064 mod-97-10 check digits. Returns the verdict with a specific failure reason, the electronic and print formats, and the decomposed bank code, branch code and account number according to that country's registered layout. Covers the 89 countries of the SWIFT IBAN registry. Structure and checksum only, it does not confirm the account exists.

params.name: iban
params.description: The IBAN. Spaces and non-breaking spaces are stripped; lowercase is accepted and uppercased.
params.expected: an IBAN of at most 64 characters

routes.output: valid (boolean), iban (electronic format, no spaces, uppercase), iban_print (grouped in fours), country (first two characters), check_digits, bban, parts ({bank, branch, account}, each string|null per the registry layout for the country; all null when the length, structure or country is wrong), length (actual), expected_length (registry length, null for an unknown country), reason (null | country_unknown | length | charset | structure | checksum, checked in that order), algorithm (always mod-97-10). A failed verdict is a 200, never a 400.

sources.attribution: IBAN registry via ibantools (MIT); field offsets via schwifty (MIT); underlying data: SWIFT IBAN Registry, public

routes.name: iban-build
routes.summary: Construct an IBAN from a country code and BBAN or bank/branch/account, computing mod-97-10
routes.description: Construct an IBAN from a country code and the domestic account parts, computing the ISO 7064 mod-97-10 check digits. Takes either a single BBAN string or named parts (bank code, branch code, account number); digit fields are left-padded with zeros to the country's registered widths. Returns the IBAN in electronic and print formats with its bank, branch and account parts. Covers the 89 SWIFT registry countries. Named parts work only where they span the whole BBAN; otherwise pass the BBAN.

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code in the SWIFT IBAN registry, case-insensitive.
params.expected: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in the IBAN registry

params.name: bban
params.description: The whole domestic account number (BBAN), alphanumeric. Use this or bank plus account.
params.expected: an alphanumeric BBAN of at most 34 characters

params.name: bank
params.description: Bank code. Requires account.
params.expected: a bank code of at most 16 characters

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch code, for countries whose layout has a branch field.
params.expected: a branch code of at most 16 characters

params.name: account
params.description: Account number. Requires bank.
params.expected: an account number of at most 32 characters

routes.output: iban (electronic format, no spaces), iban_print (grouped in fours), country, check_digits, bban, parts ({bank, branch, account} as parsed by the registry layout, each string|null: null where the country's registry layout defines no such field, e.g. branch for most countries and all three for HN), length, valid (always true on success: a built IBAN is valid by construction). Named parts are accepted only for countries where bank, branch and account together cover the whole BBAN (56 of 89); for the others (e.g. FR, ES, IT, BE with national check digits) pass bban. Digit fields shorter than their width are left-padded with zeros; letter fields must be exact.

sources.attribution: IBAN registry via ibantools (MIT); field offsets via schwifty (MIT); underlying data: SWIFT IBAN Registry, public

routes.name: zone
routes.summary: Instant to wall-clock time in an IANA zone, with offset and DST state
routes.description: Convert an instant to wall-clock time in a named IANA time zone, or a wall-clock time in a zone back to an instant. Returns the local date and time, the UTC offset in ±HH:MM and seconds, the zone abbreviation, whether DST is in effect, the ISO week date, and the day of year. Handles the ambiguous and skipped local times at DST boundaries explicitly rather than guessing.

params.name: zone
params.description: IANA time zone id, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam.
params.expected: an IANA time zone id, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam

params.name: instant
params.description: RFC 3339 timestamp or integer Unix seconds/milliseconds. Defaults to now. Mutually exclusive with local.

params.name: local
params.description: Wall-clock time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] in zone, converted back to an instant. Mutually exclusive with instant.

params.name: ambiguous
params.description: Only with local: which instant a repeated local time maps to. Default earlier.

routes.output: zone, instant (RFC 3339 UTC), epoch_ms, local (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), offset (+HH:MM), offset_seconds, abbreviation, dst, weekday, iso_week {year, week, weekday}, day_of_year, ambiguity (null|repeated|skipped), resolution (null|the ambiguous mode applied), gap (true when a skipped local time was moved forward by the gap length). abbreviation is the runtime (Intl en-US) short name, e.g. GMT+2 or EDT.

routes.name: dst
routes.summary: Next daylight-saving transitions for an IANA time zone
routes.description: List the daylight-saving transitions for an IANA time zone over a date range: the exact instant of each shift, the offset before and after, and whether local clocks jump forward or back. Returns the current offset and DST state, and the next transition from a given instant. Zones without DST return an empty transition list rather than an error.

params.name: zone
params.description: IANA time zone id.
params.expected: an IANA time zone id, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam

params.name: from
params.description: Start of the range: RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Default now.

params.name: years
params.description: Length of the range in years, 1-10. Default 2.

routes.output: zone, observes_dst, current {offset, offset_seconds, abbreviation, dst}, next (first transition after from, or null), transitions [{at, local_before, local_after, offset_before, offset_after, delta_seconds, direction forward|back, abbreviation_before, abbreviation_after}].

routes.name: business-days
routes.summary: Business-day arithmetic with a caller-supplied weekend mask and holiday list
routes.description: Business-day arithmetic with a caller-supplied calendar: add or subtract N working days from a date, or count the working days between two dates. The weekend is a weekday mask (Friday-Saturday and Sunday-only weeks work) and holidays are an explicit date list, so nothing depends on a stale holiday table. Returns the result date, the day count and the skipped dates with reasons. The skipped list is capped at 1,000 entries (skipped_truncated flags it); skipped_total is always exact.

params.name: op
params.description: add (default) N business days to from, or count business days between from and to.

params.name: from
params.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: days
params.description: Business days to add, -3650 to 3650. Required when op=add.

params.name: to
params.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD, may precede from. Required when op=count.

params.name: weekend
params.description: Comma-separated weekday names or ISO numbers. Default sat,sun. Empty string = no weekend.
params.expected: comma-separated weekday names (mon..sun) or ISO numbers 1-7

params.name: holidays
params.description: Comma-separated YYYY-MM-DD holiday dates.
params.expected: comma-separated YYYY-MM-DD dates, at most 2048 characters

params.name: inclusive
params.description: For op=count: start (default, half-open [from, to)), both or neither.

routes.output: add: result (YYYY-MM-DD), from, days, calendar_days_spanned, skipped [{date, reason weekend|holiday, weekday}] (first 1,000), skipped_total, skipped_truncated. count: business_days, calendar_days, weekend_days, holiday_days, holidays_matched, direction (forward|backward) (holidays on a weekend are reported as weekend, never as holiday). count is half-open [from, to) unless inclusive says otherwise; when to precedes from the same interval is counted backwards and business_days is still a non-negative count. skipped is in the order the dates were traversed and lists at most 1,000 entries; skipped_total is the full count and skipped_truncated is true when the list was cut (the cap only binds for days beyond roughly 1,400 working-day skips, e.g. days near 3,650 with a two-day weekend); result, calendar_days_spanned and skipped_total are always exact.

routes.name: rrule
routes.summary: RFC 5545 RRULE expansion into concrete occurrence timestamps
routes.description: Expand an RFC 5545 recurrence rule into concrete occurrence timestamps. Accepts an RRULE string with DTSTART, an IANA time zone, and optional EXDATE and RDATE lists, and returns up to 200 occurrences as both local wall-clock times and UTC instants. Supports FREQ, INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, BYSETPOS and WKST. Occurrences moved by a DST gap carry gap: true. Rules needing over 50,000 candidate evaluations are rejected.

params.name: rrule
params.description: RFC 5545 RRULE, e.g. FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR;COUNT=6.

params.name: dtstart
params.description: First occurrence, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS local to zone.

params.name: zone
params.description: IANA time zone id.
params.expected: an IANA time zone id, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam

params.name: count
params.description: Maximum occurrences to return, 1-200. Default 20.

params.name: after
params.description: RFC 3339 instant; skip occurrences before it.

params.name: exdate
params.description: Comma-separated local datetimes to exclude.

params.name: rdate
params.description: Comma-separated local datetimes to add.

routes.output: occurrences [{local, instant, epoch_ms, offset, dst, gap (present, true, only when a DST gap shifted the occurrence forward)}], count, truncated, rule (the parsed rule: freq, interval (integer), wkst, and, when given, count, until, byday [], bymonthday [], bymonth [], bysetpos [], byhour [], byminute [], bysecond []), zone.

routes.name: calendar
routes.summary: Gregorian conversion to Hijri, Hebrew and Japanese-era dates, plus Easter
routes.description: Convert a Gregorian date to other calendar systems: Islamic (both the tabular civil calendar and the Umm al-Qura variant), Hebrew, Japanese imperial era, Republic of China, Buddhist and Persian. Also computes Easter Sunday for a year in both the Gregorian and Julian reckonings. Uses the calendar support built into the runtime, with the algorithm named in every response.

params.name: op
params.description: convert (default) a Gregorian date, or easter for a year.

params.name: date
params.description: Gregorian date YYYY-MM-DD. Required when op=convert.

params.name: to
params.description: Comma-separated calendar ids: islamic, islamic-umalqura, hebrew, japanese, roc, buddhist, persian. Default all.
params.expected: islamic, islamic-umalqura, hebrew, japanese, roc, buddhist, persian

params.name: year
params.description: Year for op=easter, 326-9999.

params.name: rite
params.description: Easter reckoning: western (default) or eastern.

routes.output: convert: gregorian, calendars {<id>: {year, month, month_name, day, era, formatted, algorithm}}, and unavailable {<id>: reason} when no to was given and a calendar is undefined for the date. Gregorian input covers years 1-9999 (proleptic Gregorian, so month and month_name always agree with the date given); every field is computed for the whole range, never clamped. A calendar that is undefined for the date is rejected with 400 INVALID_PARAM on date when named in to, and listed in unavailable when to is omitted: japanese before Meiji 1 (1868-10-23) and islamic-umalqura outside its published table (1300-1600 AH, 1882-11-12 to 2174-11-25). islamic and persian are proleptic before their epoch (year 0 and negative years, as ICU computes them). easter: year, rite, date (always the Gregorian date), gregorian_date, julian_date (eastern rite only: the date in the Julian calendar), algorithm (anonymous-gregorian|meeus-julian). islamic is the tabular civil calendar; Hebrew months are numbered from Tishri = 1.

routes.name: slug
routes.summary: Unicode-aware URL slug with transliteration
routes.description: Turn arbitrary text into a URL-safe slug. Decomposes accents, transliterates German umlauts, Scandinavian and Turkish letters, the ligatures that lose meaning under plain NFD, and Cyrillic (Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Macedonian; language from lang or inferred from the letters). Lowercases, collapses separators, truncates on a word boundary. Returns the slug plus what was removed.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to slugify, at most 2048 characters.

params.name: separator
params.description: Separator: - (default), _, . or empty.

params.name: max
params.description: Maximum slug length 1-512, default 96. Truncates at the last complete word.

params.name: case
params.description: lower (default), preserve or upper.

params.name: lang
params.description: ISO 639-1 code for locale-sensitive folding (de: ü->ue) and the Cyrillic table (ru, uk, be, bg, sr, mk). Default locale-neutral; for Cyrillic the language is then inferred from letters unique to Ukrainian, Belarusian, Serbian or Macedonian, else Russian BGN/PCGN letters with ISO 9 (accents folded) for the rest.

routes.output: slug, length, truncated, source_length, transliterated [{from, to}] for every mapped character, removed (characters dropped entirely, deduplicated; includes the Cyrillic soft and hard signs and the Ukrainian apostrophe). Cyrillic: Ukrainian follows the 2010 national system (Київ Україна -> kyiv-ukraina); Belarusian, Bulgarian, Serbian and Macedonian use ASCII slug tables; Russian letters use BGN/PCGN (Привет -> privet); other Cyrillic letters use ISO 9:1995 without diacritics.

routes.name: transliterate
routes.summary: Cyrillic-to-Latin transliteration (ISO 9:1995, BGN/PCGN Russian)
routes.description: Transliterate Cyrillic text into Latin using a named standard: ISO 9:1995 (one-to-one, with diacritics, covering the full standard: Russian, other Slavic, historic and non-Slavic Cyrillic letters) or BGN/PCGN, which is the Russian system only (Ukrainian, Serbian and other letters are passed through unmapped). Returns the transliteration, the source script, the standard, the mapped fraction and the unmapped characters. Other scripts are rejected with UNSUPPORTED_VALUE.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to transliterate, at most 2048 characters.

params.name: from
params.description: Source script name (cyrillic), or auto (default).

params.name: standard
params.description: Romanisation standard: iso-9 (default; all ISO 9:1995 Cyrillic letters) or bgn-pcgn (BGN/PCGN Russian system, Russian letters only).
params.expected: iso-9 or bgn-pcgn (Russian letters only) for cyrillic

params.name: case
params.description: preserve (default), lower or upper.

routes.output: result, source_script (Unicode script name; Latin when the text has no Cyrillic, which is returned unchanged), standard (string: the validated standard, iso-9 by default; on text with no Cyrillic it is echoed although no character needed converting), coverage (0-1 fraction of non-ASCII characters mapped), unmapped (characters passed through). iso-9 maps every letter of ISO 9:1995 (Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Serbian, Macedonian, Bulgarian, historic and non-Slavic Cyrillic, e.g. і -> ì, ѣ -> ě, ә -> a̋, қ -> k̦); a base letter plus combining marks is one unit. bgn-pcgn is the Russian system only: other Cyrillic letters are returned unmapped and lower coverage.

sources.version: ISO 9:1995 (full Cyrillic repertoire) and BGN/PCGN Russian system

routes.name: unicode
routes.summary: Unicode normalisation, script detection and confusable/homoglyph analysis
routes.description: Analyse a string at the Unicode level: apply NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD, report which forms it is already in, list the scripts present (all Unicode scripts), and flag confusable and homoglyph characters — Cyrillic а in a Latin word, fullwidth or mathematical look-alikes, all-look-alike words — plus zero-width joiners, bidirectional overrides, invisible and blank characters. Returns per-character detail with code points, names and the ASCII character each imitates.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to analyse, at most 1024 characters.

params.name: form
params.description: Normalisation form to apply, default nfc.

params.name: detail
params.description: summary (default) or full per-code-point detail (capped at 256 entries).

routes.output: normalised, form, already_normalised {nfc, nfd, nfkc, nfkd}, lengths {code_points, graphemes, utf8_bytes, utf16_units} (of the normalised output), scripts (every Unicode Script property value present, from Unicode 18 Scripts.txt; Common and Inherited are not listed), mixed_script, suspicious [{index (code point index in the input), char, code_point, name (Unicode character name; string|null, null only when the name is not vendored: only ASCII, Latin-1, spaces, combining marks, format and default-ignorable characters, controls and confusable look-alikes have names), category, kind confusable|invisible|bidi|combining_excess, looks_like (string|null, null unless kind is confusable)}], ascii_safe (input is printable ASCII only); with detail=full also characters [{index, char, code_point, name (string|null, as above), category, script (string|null, null for Common/Inherited/unassigned)}] (first 256) and characters_truncated. Confusables (UTS #39 confusables.txt, the entries that map to one ASCII character): in mixed-script text every one is reported; in single-script text the compatibility look-alikes of ASCII letters and digits (fullwidth, mathematical, Roman numerals) and words written wholly in one non-Latin script whose every letter has an ASCII look-alike (whole-script confusables, e.g. Cyrillic рау). Invisible = format characters (Cf), Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (e.g. Hangul filler U+3164, variation selectors) and U+2800 braille blank; bidi = embeddings, overrides, isolates and directional marks; combining_excess = the 4th and later combining marks in a row.

routes.name: similarity
routes.summary: String distance and phonetic keys: Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Soundex, Metaphone
routes.description: Compare two strings and return every standard similarity measure in one call: Levenshtein and Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance, normalised similarity, Jaro and Jaro-Winkler, longest common subsequence, Dice coefficient on character bigrams, and the Soundex, Metaphone and NYSIIS phonetic keys of each string. Optional case folding, accent folding and whitespace normalisation before comparison.

params.name: a
params.description: First string, at most 512 characters.

params.name: b
params.description: Second string, at most 512 characters.

params.name: fold
params.description: Comma-separated folds before comparing: case, accents, space, punct. Default case.
params.expected: comma-separated subset of case, accents, space, punct

params.name: only
params.description: Comma-separated measure names to compute: levenshtein, damerau_levenshtein, normalised_similarity, jaro, jaro_winkler, lcs_length, dice, phonetic (all three keys), soundex, metaphone, nysiis. Default all.
params.expected: comma-separated subset of levenshtein, damerau_levenshtein, normalised_similarity, jaro, jaro_winkler, lcs_length, dice, phonetic, soundex, metaphone, nysiis

routes.output: levenshtein, damerau_levenshtein, normalised_similarity (0-1), jaro, jaro_winkler, lcs_length, dice, phonetic {a: {soundex, metaphone, nysiis}, b: {...}} (Soundex, Metaphone and NYSIIS are computed exactly as the jellyfish library does, on the folded string; with only=soundex|metaphone|nysiis just that key), equal_after_fold, folded {a, b}.

routes.name: url
routes.summary: URL parse, canonicalise, and registrable-domain (eTLD+1) extraction
routes.description: Parse and canonicalise a URL, and extract its registrable domain using the Public Suffix List — the part an agent needs to decide whether two URLs belong to the same owner. Returns scheme, host, port, path, decoded query parameters and fragment, the public suffix, the registrable domain (eTLD+1), the subdomain, whether the suffix is an ICANN or a private entry, plus a canonical form with default port, dot-segments and percent-encoding normalised. unicode_host uses WHATWG/UTS 46 (non-strict).

params.name: url
params.description: Absolute URL, or a bare hostname (https:// assumed).
params.expected: an absolute URL, or a hostname

params.name: base
params.description: Base URL to resolve url against as a relative reference.

routes.output: canonical, scheme, username (string|null, null without userinfo), host (string|null; null for absolute URLs with no host such as mailto:, urn:, data: and file:///, which parse per WHATWG with path holding everything after the scheme; for those public_suffix, registrable_domain, subdomain, host_type and unicode_host are null and suffix_source is none), port (null when default), path, fragment (string|null, null without a fragment), query [{key, value}], public_suffix (string|null, null for IP hosts), registrable_domain (eTLD+1; string|null, null when public_suffix is null or the host is the suffix itself), subdomain (string|null, null when there is none), suffix_source (icann|private|none), host_type (domain|ipv4|ipv6|idn; null without a host), unicode_host (string|null, null when the host is not an IDN).

routes.name: idn
routes.summary: IDNA2008 / punycode conversion and domain-label validation
routes.description: Convert internationalised domain names between Unicode and ASCII punycode in either direction, label by label, and validate each label against IDNA2008: length, leading and trailing hyphens, the hyphen-hyphen rule at positions 3 and 4, disallowed code points and bidirectional rules. Returns both forms, the per-label breakdown and the first rule violated. Strict mode is IDNA2008 (UTS 46 non-transitional); it may reject names /v1/code/url displays.

params.name: domain
params.description: Domain name in Unicode or punycode form.

params.name: to
params.description: ascii, unicode or both (default). Validated only: the response always carries both forms.

params.name: strict
params.description: true (default) applies IDNA2008 strictly; false uses UTS 46 transitional (IDNA2003-compatible) processing, which maps e.g. ß to ss; current browsers and /v1/code/url use non-transitional processing, so its output can differ from them.

routes.output: ascii (string|null, null only when a label cannot be converted at all, e.g. a disallowed code point; a label that merely breaks a hyphen rule is still converted, valid:false), unicode (string|null, same), valid, labels [{index, unicode, ascii (string|null), length (integer|null, null when the label cannot be converted), punycoded, valid, reason (string|null)}], reason (first failure or null), total_length (integer|null, null when a label cannot be converted).

sources.attribution: Unicode IdnaMappingTable via the tr46 package (MIT); (c) Unicode, Inc.

routes.name: semver
routes.summary: Semantic-version parse, compare, and range satisfaction
routes.description: Parse a semantic version into major, minor, patch, prerelease and build parts; compare two versions by precedence including prerelease ordering; or test whether a version satisfies a range expression using caret, tilde, hyphen, x-ranges and comparator sets. Returns the parsed structure, the comparison result and the reason a range did not match.

params.name: op
params.description: parse (default), compare, satisfies or sort.

params.name: version
params.description: Version to parse (op=parse) or test (op=satisfies).

params.name: a
params.description: First version for op=compare.

params.name: b
params.description: Second version for op=compare.

params.name: range
params.description: Range expression for op=satisfies, e.g. ^1.2.0.

params.name: versions
params.description: Comma-separated versions for op=sort, at most 100.

routes.output: parse: valid, major, minor, patch (integers; null when the version is invalid), prerelease [], build [], is_prerelease, canonical (string|null, null when invalid), reason (string|null: why an invalid version failed; null when valid). compare: result (-1|0|1), a, b, precedence_note. satisfies: satisfies, range (normalised by node-semver; the trimmed input when that is empty, as for * and x), comparators [], reason. sort: sorted [], invalid [].

routes.name: hash
routes.summary: SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE2 and HMAC digests of supplied text or base64 bytes
routes.description: Compute a cryptographic digest of supplied data: SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-1, SHA3-256, SHA3-512, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b-256 and BLAKE2b-512, plus HMAC with any of them. Input is UTF-8 text, base64 or hex bytes; output is hex, base64, base64url or base32. Returns the digest, the byte length of the input, and the exact algorithm identifier used.

params.name: algo
params.description: Digest algorithm.
params.expected: sha256, sha384, sha512, sha1, sha3-256, sha3-512, keccak256, blake2b-256, blake2b-512

params.name: data
params.description: Input data, interpreted per encoding. At most 8192 characters. An empty value hashes the empty string.

params.name: encoding
params.description: Encoding of data: utf8 (default), base64, base64url or hex.

params.name: out
params.description: Digest output encoding: hex (default), base64, base64url or base32.

params.name: hmac_key
params.description: If present, computes HMAC with this key.

params.name: hmac_key_encoding
params.description: Encoding of hmac_key, as encoding.

routes.output: digest, algo, out, input_bytes, hmac (boolean), bit_length.

routes.name: jwt
routes.summary: JWT structural decode: header, claims, expiry state — no signature verification
routes.description: Decode a JSON Web Token without verifying it: returns the header, the claims, the signature length and algorithm, and a computed view of the time claims — whether exp has passed, whether nbf is in the future, and the remaining lifetime in seconds against a supplied or current instant. Reports structural problems such as a missing part, invalid base64url or an alg of none. It does not and cannot verify the signature; do not use it to decide trust.

params.name: token
params.description: The JWT to decode (not verified). At most 8192 characters.

params.name: at
params.description: Instant to evaluate exp/nbf against: RFC 3339 or epoch seconds. Default now.

routes.output: valid_structure, header and payload (the decoded JSON objects echoed exactly as sent, including non-conforming values; null when absent or not an object), alg, typ, kid (each string|null: null when the header lacks it or it is not a string), signature_bytes, parts, claims {iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, iat, jti} (the RFC 7519 registered claims, normalised: iss, sub and jti are strings, aud is a string or an array of strings, exp, nbf and iat are numbers; each is null when absent or when its value does not conform), claim_errors [{claim, reason}] (present only when a registered claim did not conform and was nulled in claims, e.g. aud: 5 or exp: "soon"), time {evaluated_at, expired (boolean|null, null without a conforming exp), not_yet_valid (boolean|null, null without a conforming nbf), expires_in_seconds (integer|null, null without a conforming exp), age_seconds (integer|null, null without a conforming iat)}, signature_verified (always false), warnings [], reason.

header.description: caller-supplied content echoed exactly as decoded: members are not typed

payload.description: caller-supplied content echoed exactly as decoded: members are not typed

aud.description: RFC 7519 4.1.3: string or array of strings; null when absent

routes.name: geohash
routes.summary: Geohash encode and decode with neighbour cells
routes.description: Encode a WGS-84 latitude and longitude to a geohash at a chosen precision, or decode a geohash back to its bounding box, centre point and error bounds in metres. Encoding also returns the eight neighbouring cells, which is what a caller needs to do proximity search over a geohash-indexed store without a spatial database.

params.name: op
params.description: encode (default): lat/lon to geohash. decode: geohash to bounding box.

params.name: lat
params.description: WGS-84 latitude, -90 to 90. Required when op=encode.

params.name: lon
params.description: WGS-84 longitude, -180 to 180. Required when op=encode.

params.name: precision
params.description: Geohash length 1-12, default 9 (about 4.8 m).

params.name: geohash
params.description: Geohash to decode, 1-12 characters. Required when op=decode.
params.expected: base32 geohash alphabet, excluding a, i, l and o

routes.output: encode: geohash, precision, bbox {min_lat, min_lon, max_lat, max_lon}, center {lat, lon}, error_m {lat, lon}, neighbours {n, ne, e, se, s, sw, w, nw} (each string|null: null where the cell would lie beyond a pole). decode: the same without neighbours, plus cell_width_m, cell_height_m (metres on WGS-84). Neighbour cells that would lie beyond a pole are null; longitude wraps at the antimeridian.

routes.name: pluscode
routes.summary: Open Location Code (plus code) encode and decode
routes.description: Encode coordinates as an Open Location Code (plus code) at a chosen length, or decode a full code back to its bounding box and centre. Also shortens a full code against a reference coordinate and recovers a shortened code given a reference, which is how plus codes are normally exchanged in text. Returns code length, precision in metres and validity.

params.name: op
params.description: encode (default), decode, shorten or recover.

params.name: lat
params.description: Latitude for op=encode.

params.name: lon
params.description: Longitude for op=encode.

params.name: code
params.description: Plus code for decode, shorten or recover.

params.name: length
params.description: Integer code length for op=encode: one of 2,4,6,8,10 (default),11,12,13,14,15. Other integers in 2-15 are 400 UNSUPPORTED_VALUE.

params.name: ref_lat
params.description: Reference latitude for op=shorten/recover.

params.name: ref_lon
params.description: Reference longitude for op=shorten/recover.

routes.output: code, length (integer|null, null for an invalid code), bbox {min_lat, min_lon, max_lat, max_lon}, center {lat, lon}, precision_m (cell height in metres, rounded to 0.1), is_full, is_short, valid, reason (string|null, null on success). Invalid codes on op=decode return 200 with valid:false and a reason (invalid character is checked before the + position); short codes decode to valid:true, is_short:true without a bbox. shorten also returns full_code. shorten/recover with a malformed code are 400 INVALID_PARAM.

routes.name: polygon
routes.summary: Point-in-polygon, bounding box, centroid and area on supplied GeoJSON
routes.description: Geometric predicates on a GeoJSON geometry supplied in the request: point-in-polygon with correct hole handling, bounding box, centroid, signed area in square metres, perimeter length, and ring winding order. Accepts Polygon and MultiPolygon, and a GeoJSON Feature wrapping either. Area and length are geodesic on the WGS-84 ellipsoid, correct at any latitude; containment is planar in lon/lat.

params.name: geometry
params.description: URL-encoded GeoJSON Polygon, MultiPolygon or a Feature wrapping one. At most 3072 characters and 2000 coordinate pairs.

params.name: lat
params.description: Point latitude; with lon, runs the containment test.

params.name: lon
params.description: Point longitude; with lat, runs the containment test.

params.name: ops
params.description: Comma-separated subset of contains,bbox,centroid,area,perimeter,winding. Default all.
params.expected: comma-separated subset of contains, bbox, centroid, area, perimeter, winding

routes.output: contains (boolean|null), on_boundary (boolean|null), bbox [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat], centroid {lat, lon}, area_m2, perimeter_m, winding (cw|ccw per ring, exterior first then holes, in polygon order), rings, vertices (closing point excluded). area_m2 is the WGS-84 geodesic area, signed per RFC 7946 (exterior counter-clockwise = positive, clockwise = negative, holes subtract); perimeter_m sums every ring. Point-in-polygon and centroid are planar in lon/lat; a point on an edge is contained with on_boundary:true. With ops, only the listed fields (plus rings and vertices) are returned. Rings must be closed with at least 4 positions.

routes.name: distance
routes.summary: Geodesic distance, initial bearing and destination point on WGS-84
routes.description: Distance and direction between WGS-84 coordinates: geodesic distance by Vincenty with a haversine fallback, initial and final bearing, the midpoint, and the destination point reached from a start point on a given bearing and distance. Also computes the cumulative length of a supplied coordinate path. Results in metres, kilometres, nautical miles and miles.

params.name: op
params.description: distance (default), destination, midpoint or path.

params.name: lat1
params.description: Start latitude.

params.name: lon1
params.description: Start longitude.

params.name: lat2
params.description: End latitude.

params.name: lon2
params.description: End longitude.

params.name: bearing
params.description: Initial bearing in degrees for op=destination.

params.name: distance_m
params.description: Distance in metres for op=destination, 0 to 1e9 (about 25 Earth circumferences); larger values are 400 INVALID_PARAM.

params.name: path
params.description: Comma-separated lat,lon pairs for op=path, at most 200 points.
params.expected: comma-separated lat,lon pairs, at most 200 points

params.name: method
params.description: vincenty (default, WGS-84) or haversine.

routes.output: op=distance and op=midpoint: distance {m, km, nmi, mi}, bearing_initial, bearing_final (degrees clockwise from north, 4 dp), midpoint {lat, lon} (geodesic midpoint; spherical when method is haversine), method, converged. Vincenty on WGS-84 is used unless method=haversine (R = 6,371,008.8 m); when Vincenty fails to converge (near-antipodal pairs) the response falls back to haversine and reports method:"haversine", converged:false. op=destination: destination {lat, lon} (longitude wrapped to -180..180; Karney's direct algorithm on WGS-84, or spherical with R = 6,371,008.8 m when method=haversine), bearing_final (also for method=haversine, on the sphere), method, converged. op=path: distance {m, km, nmi, mi}, points, legs, method (vincenty, haversine, or vincenty+haversine if any leg fell back), converged. path is a flat comma list lat,lon,lat,lon,... (semicolons or spaces also separate pairs); it needs at least 2 points.

routes.name: address
routes.summary: Blockchain address format detection and checksum validation
routes.description: Identify which blockchain an address belongs to and validate its encoding: EVM EIP-55 checksum, Bitcoin base58check and bech32/bech32m with witness version, Solana base58 and on-curve check, Cosmos bech32 with its HRP, Tron, XRP, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Cardano, Polkadot SS58 and Algorand. Returns every chain the address is valid for (ambiguous when several match), the checksummed form for EVM addresses, and the reason a check failed, including unrecognised_format.

params.name: address
params.description: Address to identify and validate.

params.name: expect
params.description: Restrict the check to one chain id.
params.expected: evm, bitcoin, solana, cosmos, tron, xrp, cardano, polkadot, algorand, litecoin, dogecoin

params.name: chain_id
params.description: EVM chain id; enables EIP-1191 chain-salted checksum validation.

routes.output: valid, matches [{chain, format (string|null), valid, reason (string|null), detail (members depend on the format: hrp, witness_version, encoding for bech32 (cosmos adds bytes); version_byte, purpose for base58check; on_curve for Solana; address_type, header_type, network for Cardano; network_prefix for SS58)}], checksum ({input_form, checksummed, checksum_valid, eip1191_applied} for EVM, else null), ambiguous, reason (present only when the whole input failed: expect_mismatch when expect= was given and no match has that chain, unrecognised_format when no detector recognises the input and no match is listed).

routes.name: selector
routes.summary: Keccak-256 hash, 4-byte function selector and 32-byte event topic from a Solidity signature
routes.description: Compute the Keccak-256 hash of a Solidity function or event signature and derive the 4-byte function selector and the 32-byte event topic. Normalises the signature first — strips parameter names, expands uint to uint256 and the other aliases, flattens tuples — so a signature copied from source code produces the same selector as the canonical form. Also hashes arbitrary text or hex bytes with Keccak-256.

params.name: signature
params.description: Solidity function, event or error signature, e.g. transfer(address to, uint amount).

params.name: data
params.description: Alternative to signature: raw data to Keccak-256 hash.

params.name: encoding
params.description: Encoding of data: utf8 (default) or hex.

params.name: kind
params.description: function (default), event or error.

routes.output: canonical (string|null, null in data mode), keccak256 (0x + 32 bytes), selector (0x + 4 bytes; string|null, null for kind=event and in data mode), topic0 (0x + 32 bytes; string|null, null for kind=function or error and in data mode), inputs ([] or null, null in data mode), normalisations [{from, to}]. Data mode (data= instead of signature, hashing arbitrary text or hex bytes with Keccak-256): canonical, selector, topic0 and inputs are null, normalisations is empty, and encoding (utf8|hex) and input_bytes (integer) are added.

routes.name: nuts
routes.summary: NUTS statistical region code lookup for the EU
routes.description: Look up a NUTS statistical region of the European Union: resolve a NUTS code to its name, country and level, walk up to its parents or down to its children, or search regions by name. Covers all four levels (country, major region, basic region, small region) for the 27 member states and 12 further reporting countries, from the NUTS 2024 classification. Returns the Latin-script and local-language names plus the urbanisation, coastal and mountain typologies.

params.name: code
params.description: NUTS code, 2-5 characters, case-insensitive (level-3 codes may contain letters, e.g. NL32B). A GR or GB prefix is accepted for EL or UK.

params.name: name
params.description: Substring search on region names, case- and accent-insensitive. Up to 25 matches.

params.name: level
params.description: Restrict a name search to one level, 0-3.

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country filter (UK/GB and EL/GR both accepted).

params.name: include
params.description: Comma-separated: parents, children, typology. Default parents,typology.
params.expected: comma-separated subset of parents, children, typology

routes.output: found, code, level, country, name_latn, name_local, parents [{code, level, name_latn}] from level 0 down to the parent, children [{code, level, name_latn}] (direct children, sorted by code; only when include has children), typology {urban, urban_label, coastal, coastal_label, mountain, mountain_label} (codes are Eurostat typology codes as strings, null where unclassified; labels follow Eurostat's published typology definitions). Keys not named in include are omitted. A name search returns matches [{code, level, country, name_latn, name_local}] (exact name first, then by level and code) plus total_matches. NUTS uses EL and UK for Greece and the United Kingdom; country and the code prefix accept GR and GB as aliases; found responses carry canonical_country (the NUTS spelling, EL or UK for those two) and input_code (the alias as sent) when an alias was mapped.

routes.name: airport
routes.summary: Airport lookup by IATA or ICAO code with coordinates and elevation
routes.description: Look up an airport by IATA or ICAO code and get its name, city, country, ISO 3166-2 region code, WGS-84 coordinates, elevation and IANA time zone, or find the nearest airports to a coordinate within a radius. Covers every airport worldwide that holds a three-letter IATA code and scheduled service. Returns the code type that matched and the distance in kilometres for proximity results.

params.name: code
params.description: 3-letter IATA or 4-letter ICAO code, case-insensitive.

params.name: near
params.description: lat,lon to search around.

params.name: radius_km
params.description: Search radius in km, 1-1000, default 100. Only with near.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum results 1-25, default 5. Only with near.

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 filter.

routes.output: found, matched_on (iata|icao), airport {iata, icao, name, municipality, country, region, lat, lon, elevation_ft (number|null, null when OurAirports has no elevation, 129 airports), type, timezone}, nearby (for near: the same plus distance_km and bearing_deg, nearest first; distance is haversine on a 6,371.0088 km sphere, bearing is the initial bearing in degrees from the query point; matched_on is absent). A code matches IATA (3 characters) first, then ICAO/local identifier. found is false for an unknown code or an empty nearby list. timezone is the IANA zone of the airport location, derived offline at build time from its coordinates (timezone-boundary-builder 2026d); it is the geographic zone, not an airline convention (Xinjiang airports read Asia/Urumqi, UTC+6, although flights run on Beijing time). Coordinates on a zone border can resolve to the neighbouring zone (Gold Coast OOL reads Australia/Sydney).

sources.attribution: Time zones derived from timezone-boundary-builder data (https://github.com/evansiroky/timezone-boundary-builder), (c) contributors, ODbL 1.0, via timezonefinder 9.0.0

routes.name: currency
routes.summary: Currency record (ISO 4217 codes, names and minor units; CLDR cash rounding)
routes.description: Look up a currency by its ISO 4217 alphabetic or numeric code: the official English name, minor-unit exponent, fund flag, the smallest cash denomination where it differs from the minor unit, the territories that use it, and historic codes on request. Returns the correct rounding increment for cash amounts, which is what a caller needs to render or settle a price. This route returns currency facts only and never an exchange rate.

params.name: code
params.description: ISO 4217 alpha-3 or 3-digit numeric code.
params.expected: a 3-letter alphabetic or 3-digit numeric ISO 4217 code

params.name: country
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; returns the currencies in use there.

params.name: include
params.description: Comma-separated: territories, historic. Default none.

routes.output: found, code, numeric (3-digit string per ISO 4217; null for the three historic codes XFO, XFU, XRE), name (ISO 4217 English name, e.g. Lek, Forint, Rupiah), minor_units (ISO 4217 exponent, e.g. IDR 2, HUF 2, JPY 0, KWD 3; null where ISO lists N.A.: precious metals XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD, XDR, XXX and the other X-codes; null for historic codes), cash_minor_units (equals minor_units unless CLDR gives a cash digit count, e.g. SEK 0), cash_rounding (number|null: CLDR cash rounding increment expressed in ISO minor units, e.g. 5 for CHF and CAD means 0.05, 50 for DKK, 500 for HUF meaning 5.00; null when none), is_fund (boolean: the ISO 4217 fund flag, true for BOV, CHE, CHW, CLF, COU, MXV, USN, UYI, UYW and XAD, false otherwise), territories (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, sorted, when include has territories; territory sets come from CLDR), status (current|historic), withdrawn (ISO withdrawal date as published, usually YYYY-MM, historic codes only). Historic codes come from ISO 4217 list three and are only found with include=historic, by alphabetic or numeric code (e.g. DEM 276, ZWD 716); a code that is in both lists (EUR, RON) is current. Some numeric codes were reused by several historic codes: the most recently withdrawn code is returned and the others are listed in numeric_shared_with. With country=XX the response is {found, country, currencies: [the same record for each legal-tender currency in use there per CLDR]}. Never an exchange rate.

sources.attribution: ISO 4217 currency and funds code lists, published by SIX Group as secretariat of the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency (public data)

routes.name: country
routes.summary: ISO 3166-1 country record: codes, currency, TLD, UN M49 region, ISO 3166-2 subdivisions
routes.description: Look up a country or territory by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 or numeric code, or by name, and get the other codes, the official and common English names, the UN M49 region and sub-region, the currencies in use, the country-code top-level domain, and optionally the full ISO 3166-2 subdivision list with each subdivision's type. Also resolves an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code such as NL-NH directly. Names are matched case- and accent-insensitively.

params.name: code
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 or numeric code, or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code such as NL-NH.
params.expected: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2/alpha-3/numeric, or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code

params.name: name
params.description: Substring search on country names, case- and accent-insensitive.

params.name: include
params.description: Comma-separated: subdivisions, m49, currency, tld. Default m49,currency,tld.
params.expected: comma-separated subset of subdivisions, m49, currency, tld

routes.output: found, kind (country|subdivision), alpha_2, alpha_3, numeric, name, official_name (the ISO 3166-1 official name from Debian iso-codes, e.g. "Kingdom of the Netherlands"; the short name where ISO defines no separate official name; always a string), m49 {region, region_name, subregion, subregion_name, intermediate, intermediate_name} (UN M49 codes as zero-padded 3-character strings; subregion and intermediate are null where the hierarchy has no such level), currencies [ISO 4217 alpha-3, legal tender in use per CLDR], tld [".xx"] (the ccTLD in actual use, so GB gives .uk; empty where none is delegated), subdivision_count (always present: the number of ISO 3166-2 subdivisions), and with include=subdivisions subdivisions [{code, name, type, parent}] (ISO 3166-2 from Debian iso-codes main of 2026-09-28, source order; parent is the parent subdivision code or null; countries with none return an empty list). A code of the form CC-XXX (e.g. NL-NH) resolves a subdivision: kind is subdivision, subdivision {code, name, type, parent} is added, and the country fields describe its country. m49, currencies and tld are omitted when not named in include; subdivision_count is not. A name search adds matches [{alpha_2, alpha_3, numeric, name}] (exact name first, then substring; at most 25) plus total_matches, and the top-level fields describe the first match. ZZ and other non-ISO codes are never found.

sources.version: Debian iso-codes data/iso_3166-1.json (official_name) and data/iso_3166-2.json, retrieved 2026-09-28
sources.attribution: ISO 3166-1 official names and ISO 3166-2 subdivision data from Debian iso-codes (https://salsa.debian.org/iso-codes-team/iso-codes), (c) 2016 Dr. Tobias Quathamer, LGPL-2.1-or-later

routes.name: radix
routes.summary: Integer conversion between arbitrary numeric bases 2–36
routes.description: Convert an integer between any two numeric bases from 2 to 36, with arbitrary precision so values far beyond 2^53 are exact. Accepts an optional sign and common prefixes (0x, 0b, 0o), validates every digit against the source base, and returns the value in the target base, in decimal, and as its bit length and digit count.

params.name: value
params.description: Integer to convert; optional sign and 0x/0b/0o prefix.

params.name: from
params.description: Source base 2-36, or auto (default) to read a 0x/0b/0o prefix.

params.name: to
params.description: Target base 2-36, default 10.

params.name: case
params.description: Digit case for bases above 10: lower (default) or upper.

params.name: prefix
params.description: Emit 0x/0b/0o where conventional. Default false.

routes.output: result, decimal, from, to, negative, digits, bit_length, exact (always true).

routes.name: words
routes.summary: Number spelled out in words, 12 locales, with ordinal and currency forms
routes.description: Spell a number out in words in English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Swedish or Japanese, in cardinal, ordinal or currency form. Currency form agrees the number with the currency noun and gives real minor-unit names for 19 currencies (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN, RUB, TRY, CNY, INR, BRL, MXN, CAD, AUD, NZD, CZK, HUF); any other ISO 4217 code uses a fraction such as 56/100. Values up to 10^15.

params.name: value
params.description: Integer or decimal, absolute value below 1e15.

params.name: lang
params.description: Language, ISO 639-1. Default en.
params.expected: en, nl, de, fr, es, it, pt, pl, ru, tr, sv, ja

params.name: form
params.description: cardinal (default), ordinal, currency or year.

params.name: currency
params.description: ISO 4217 code. Required when form=currency, rejected otherwise.

params.name: case
params.description: lower (default), sentence or title.

routes.output: words (ordinals are the masculine singular nominative form, e.g. es segundo, fr deuxième, it secondo, pt segundo, pl drugi, ru второй, sv andra, tr ikinci, ja 二番目; form=year reads pl and ru as an ordinal, ja with the suffix 年, and en, nl, de and sv in hundreds; in the currency form the number agrees with the gender of the currency noun, e.g. fr une couronne, es una libra, ru одна крона, sv ett pund), value, lang, form, currency ({code, unit_singular, unit_plural, minor_singular, minor_plural, minor_units} or null; minor_singular and minor_plural are null for zero-decimal currencies and for currencies without a curated subunit name), parts ({integer_words, minor_words} for the currency form; minor_words is the subunit count in words for the 19 curated currencies (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN, RUB, TRY, CNY, INR, BRL, MXN, CAD, AUD, NZD, CZK, HUF); every other currency uses the neutral fraction <n>/<10^minor_units> with no leading zeros (10/1000, 1/100, 56/100) instead of a subunit name, and null when there is no minor part; parts is null for other forms), rounding_applied (currency form; present, true, only when surplus decimals were rounded; an amount that rounds up to 1e15 is rejected).

routes.name: stats
routes.summary: Descriptive statistics and percentiles for a supplied numeric array
routes.description: Descriptive statistics for a supplied numeric array in one call: count, sum, mean, median, mode, variance and standard deviation with variance and standard deviation honouring ddof (default 1, the sample form; 0 gives the population form) and always-population *_population fields, min, max, range, the quartiles and interquartile range, skewness, kurtosis, and any requested percentiles. Percentiles use a named interpolation method so the result is reproducible rather than implementation-defined.

params.name: values
params.description: Comma-separated finite numbers, at most 500 values.

params.name: percentiles
params.description: Comma-separated percentiles 0-100, at most 20. Default 25,50,75.

params.name: method
params.description: Percentile interpolation (NumPy/R names): linear (default), nearest, lower, higher, midpoint.

params.name: ddof
params.description: Delta degrees of freedom for variance/stdev: 1 (default, sample, n-1) or 0 (population, n). The *_population fields are always population.

routes.output:
n, sum (number|null), mean (number|null), median (number|null), mode ([] or null, null when every value is distinct), ddof (integer), variance (number|null: n-ddof divisor, null when n <= ddof), stdev (number|null, null when n <= ddof), variance_population (number|null), stdev_population (number|null), min, max, range (number|null), q1 (number|null), q3 (number|null), iqr (number|null), skewness (number|null, null when n < 3 or the variance is 0), kurtosis_excess (number|null, null when n < 4 or the variance is 0), percentiles {

: number|null}, method, outliers_tukey []. Any computed number is null when the result is not finite, i.e. overflows the double range (e.g. values=1e308,1e308)

routes.name: allocate
routes.summary: Split a money amount into shares with no rounding loss
routes.description: Split a money amount into shares without losing or inventing a cent. Divide evenly into N parts, or by a list of ratios, and the remainder is distributed one minor unit at a time by a named, deterministic rule — largest-remainder, first-wins or last-wins — so the parts always sum exactly to the original. Uses the ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent of the currency, so zero- and three-decimal currencies work (JPY 0, KWD 3); metals and XXX are rejected.

params.name: amount
params.description: Decimal amount, absolute value below 1e12.
params.expected: a decimal amount with absolute value below 1e12

params.name: currency
params.description: ISO 4217 alpha-3 code.

params.name: parts
params.description: Number of equal parts, 1-1000. One of parts or ratios.

params.name: ratios
params.description: Comma-separated non-negative ratios, at most 1000, each with at most 15 integer digits and 15 decimal places. One of parts or ratios.

params.name: rule
params.description: Remainder rule: largest-remainder (default), first, last or round-robin.

routes.output: shares [decimal strings], shares_minor [integers], total (equals amount exactly), currency, minor_units, remainder_distributed, rule.

sources.attribution: ISO 4217 currency and funds code lists, published by SIX Group as secretariat of the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency (public data)
